web_blocks.text: Executive Thesis: An Elite Certification Toll-Booth in an Extended Stage 2 Sprint

web_blocks.html: International Gemological Institute (India) Limited (NSE: IGIL) runs the world's largest independent diamond certification network. It holds ~65% global share in lab-grown diamond (LGD) grading across 36 laboratories and 21 gemological schools [3][4]. Unlike cutters or retailers, IGIL holds zero stone inventory. It converts 33.7% of revenue into free cash flow (CY24 audited) and earns 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE with virtually no debt [1][3].

In October 2025, GIA replaced granular 4Cs letter grades on LGDs with broad 'Premium' and 'Standard' labels. Global jewelers and wholesalers shifted volume to IGI's 4Cs standard [9][10]. That tailwind pushed Q2 FY27 (ended Sep 30, 2026) revenue up +31% YoY to ₹398.0 Cr on 4.35 million reports (+26% YoY). PAT jumped +43% YoY to ₹185.8 Cr, prompting management to raise FY27 revenue growth guidance from 15% to 27%+ [4][5].

Two structural features anchor this moat. First, IGIL bills on fixed carat-weight slabs and piece counts rather than a percentage of stone value. That rate-card model cushions revenue against wholesale LGD price drops. Second, its 28.5x trailing P/E sits well below domestic consumer and rating peers despite 69.2% ROCE [1][17].

Still, discipline separates what to own from when to buy. The stock jumped +38.28% in one month to ₹438.90, leaving Daily RSI at 79.69 (+27.51% above the 200-DMA). Chasing here yields poor 0.82:1 risk-reward to our ₹340 stop. Waiting for the ₹375–₹395 support zone restores a clean 2.27:1 asymmetric entry.

Following GIA's October 2025 decision to replace granular 4Cs letter grades on lab-grown diamonds with broad 'Premium' and 'Standard' labels, global wholesalers and retail chains consolidated around IGI's 4Cs standard [9][10]. That structural tailwind drove Q2 FY27 (ended Sep 30, 2026) revenue up +31% YoY to ₹398.0 Cr (4.35 million reports, +26% YoY) and PAT up +43% YoY to ₹185.8 Cr, prompting management to raise full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance from 15% to 27%+ [4][5].

book_paragraphs: Picture a transaction where neither the diamond cutter in Surat nor the bridal retailer in Dallas trusts the other's word on a one-carat stone. Between them stands a sealed plastic dossier bearing a single logo and a laser-inscribed serial number. That toll-booth belongs to International Gemological Institute.

When we audited IGIL completely blind to its stock price in Pass 1, the business passed with flying colors: 69.2% return on capital, 57%-plus operating margins, zero inventory risk, and a freshly widened moat after rival GIA stepped back from granular lab-grown 4Cs grading in October 2025.

Only after locking that fundamental conviction did we unlock the November 13, 2026 market tape. At ₹438.90, IGIL trades at a reasonable 28.5 times trailing earnings—cheaper than Titan, Kalyan, or CRISIL—but the stock has just sprinted 38.3% in a single month to a daily RSI of 79.69. Because you hold zero shares today, our job is simple: do not chase. Assign WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT, keep your marginal cash ready, and step in cleanly between ₹375 and ₹395 with a hard stop at ₹340 and a ₹520 base target.

book_subsections.title: How to Read This Dossier
paragraphs: Before we dive into the history and numbers, let me explain how this monograph is built. Chapters 1 through 6 were written in complete price-blind isolation—meaning we deliberately hid the stock price, valuation multiples, and chart patterns until the underlying business quality was judged on its own merits. Only in Chapter 7 did we unlock the market tape, test the current ₹438.90 share price against a Reverse DCF, and check whether the Stage 2 chart offers an asymmetric entry.

That two-step discipline prevents the most common mistake in equity research: falling in love with a rising stock chart and retrofitting a fundamental story to justify chasing it. By the time you reach Chapter 9, you will have every financial ratio, every competitive risk, every technical level, and a 100% reconciled capital allocation plan.

book_subsections.title: Quick Reference: What You Need to Remember
paragraphs: If you take only three numbers away from this prologue before diving into Chapter 1, remember these: 69.2% return on capital employed on a virtually debt-free balance sheet, 28.5 times trailing earnings against 27%+ guided FY27 revenue growth, and a daily RSI of 79.69 that tells us to wait patiently for ₹375 to ₹395.

Those three numbers summarize the entire investment case. The business is an elite, cash-converting global toll-booth with a widening moat in lab-grown diamonds and studded jewelry. The valuation is reasonable relative to peers like Titan, Kalyan, and CRISIL. Only the short-term tape is stretched—and because we hold zero shares today, patience costs us nothing and improves our reward-to-risk ratio from 0.82-to-1 to 2.27-to-1.
